release 0.0.9 (#48)

feat: bundle a Flyte MCP server with the plugin, and fix the MCP skill (#24)

* feat: bundle a Flyte MCP server with the plugin, and fix the MCP skill

Installing flyte-skills now also registers a Flyte MCP server, so Claude can act on
the user's cluster (run/inspect tasks, manage runs, apps, triggers) rather than only
advising about it. It is tenant-agnostic: the server calls flyte.init_from_config(),
so it targets whatever control plane the user's `flyte` CLI is already authenticated
against. Nothing is hardcoded to a cluster, which is what makes it publishable.

Why a bundled launcher script instead of the SDK's own entry point: on flyte[mcp]
<= 2.5.11 there is no working stdio transport. MCPAppEnvironment accepts
transport="stdio" and validates it, but __post_init__ builds the Starlette app and
points _server at uvicorn for every value, so "stdio" silently serves HTTP. The
script runs the environment's FastMCP object directly. flyteorg/flyte-sdk#1319 fixes
this upstream; once released, .mcp.json can call `flyte-mcp --transport stdio` and
this script goes away.

- .mcp.json + scripts/flyte_mcp_stdio.py: the bundled server, configurable by env
  var (tool groups/tools, allowlists, config/project/domain) since the file is
  plugin-managed and overwritten on update.
- Defaults to task,run,app,trigger. The `search` group is off: its tools clone two
  repos into ~/.flyte/mcp on first use, which stalls MCP startup, and the skills
  already provide docs grounding.
- The launcher fails fast when project/domain are unset. init_from_config()
  succeeds even when it finds no config file at all, after which every tool call
  fails with "project_id.domain: must be at least 1 characters" -- which reads as a
  tool bug rather than missing setup.
- scripts/smoke_test_mcp.py: spawns the server exactly as a client does, handshakes,
  and makes one read-only list_runs call.

Fixes to the flyte-mcp-server skill, which documented things that do not exist:

- It taught `claude mcp add --transport stdio ... flyte-mcp`, which cannot work on
  released versions (see above). Now version-scoped, with the HTTP path for older
  versions and native stdio for newer.
- Its tool table listed build_image, build_uv_script_image_remote,
  run_uv_script_remote, flyte_uv_script_format and flyte_uv_script_example under
  `build`/`script` groups. Those were removed in flyte-sdk v2.3.6; two code samples
  passed tool_groups=[..., "script"], which now raises Unknown tool group(s).
- Warns against `uvx --with "flyte[mcp]"`: uvx resolves the package from the command
  name, and `flyte-mcp` is an unrelated third-party project on PyPI, so --with
  installs and runs that instead of the SDK.

Also fixes flyte-sdk-author's YAML frontmatter, which had an unescaped apostrophe
inside a single-quoted scalar ("the user's constraints"). The block did not parse,
so the skill would not load.

* feat: serve search tools when no Flyte cluster is configured

The bundled MCP server refused to start without a Flyte config that set project and
domain. That is backwards for the plugin's most common first encounter: someone who
installs flyte-skills in order to *deploy their first cluster* has no config yet, and
a server that fails at startup makes the plugin look broken at exactly the moment
they are learning it. Worse, the config only appears after they run one of this
plugin's own deploy skills -- so the failure preceded its own fix.

The search tools need no cluster at all. `_search_files` is a filesystem grep over a
local corpus; it never touches flyte.remote. So the server now always starts and
picks its surface from what is actually reachable:

- not connected -> the 3 search tools, for grounding Flyte code you write
- connected     -> all 16, adding tasks, runs, apps and triggers

"Connected" requires project and domain, not merely a successful init.
init_from_config() succeeds even when it finds no config file at all, after which
every control-plane tool fails with "project_id.domain: must be at least 1
characters" -- so those tools are withheld rather than offered and left to break.

Setting FLYTE_MCP_TOOL_GROUPS or FLYTE_MCP_TOOLS still overrides the automatic
choice, and warns when control-plane tools are requested while disconnected.

The corpus is fetched through the SDK's own cache helper, which stages clones into a
.partial directory and renames atomically, so an interrupted fetch cannot leave a
half-populated cache. Measured at ~9s and 123 MB on a cold cache, reused instantly
after -- cheap enough to stop gating search behind an opt-in. A failed fetch degrades
to "no search tools" instead of taking the server down. FLYTE_MCP_NO_SEARCH skips it.

Verified both modes end to end against a real client session: disconnected serves 3
tools and search_flyte_sdk_examples returns matches; connected serves 16 and
list_runs returns live runs from the cluster.

* feat: add a hosted search server alongside the local stdio one

Search previously required the local stdio server to clone ~120 MB of corpus into
~/.flyte/mcp and needed uv and git on PATH. That is a lot of setup for "look up how
a TaskEnvironment is declared", and it is the first thing most people want.

.mcp.json now also declares `flyte-docs`, pointing at the read-only, unauthenticated
search MCP that internal-flyte-apps deploys at
flyte-mcp.apps.demo.hosted.unionai.cloud. Verified live: it answers an MCP
initialize and serves exactly the three search tools. Search now works the moment
the plugin is installed, with no local setup at all.

The tradeoff is that search queries leave the machine, so FLYTE_MCP_LOCAL_SEARCH
moves search back into the local server, offline and private.

The two servers are deliberately disjoint -- hosted owns search, stdio owns the
control plane -- because otherwise Claude sees two near-identical sets of search
tools and picks arbitrarily between them. Documented, because it is not obvious:
Claude Code manages plugin MCP servers through plugin installation rather than
/mcp, so there is no per-server toggle. Suppressing `flyte-docs` needs a
deniedMcpServers entry or disabling the plugin.

Two bugs found while building this:

- Search tools were registered from the requested tool groups, then handed paths
  that might be None if the corpus fetch failed or was skipped -- producing tools
  that exist and raise "sdk_examples_path is not configured" on every call. The
  corpus is now resolved first and search tools are only offered if it materialized.
- The first version set FLYTE_MCP_NO_SEARCH in .mcp.json's env block. That block
  overrides the inherited environment, so the documented "unset it to get local
  search" escape hatch could never work. Inverted to FLYTE_MCP_LOCAL_SEARCH as an
  opt-in, leaving the env block empty.

Verified all four states: shipped/no cluster -> 0 tools (hosted covers search),
shipped/connected -> 13, LOCAL_SEARCH/no cluster -> 3, LOCAL_SEARCH/connected -> 16.

* refactor: rename the plugin from flyte-skills to flyte

"flyte-skills" described the plugin when it was 15 SKILL.md files. It now also ships
two MCP servers, so the name undersells it and will keep drifting as more non-skill
components land. `/plugin install flyte@flyte` also reads better than
`flyte-skills@flyte-skills`.

Doing it now because it stops being cheap after this ships. A user's enabledPlugins
entry is keyed by plugin name and persists across updates and reinstalls, so renaming
later would make the plugin silently vanish for anyone who had installed it. The repo
is a month old with no releases, so effectively nobody is affected today.

The rename lands differently per harness, which is why it touches both the manifests
and the directory:

- Claude Code and Codex read the plugin manifests, so the *name* is their interface.
- Hermes, opencode and pi install skills by *directory path*, so plugins/flyte-skills
  -> plugins/flyte changes their documented install commands.

Also renames the stdio MCP server `flyte` -> `flyte-cluster`. The plugin name becomes
the MCP tool namespace, so leaving it would have produced tools called
mcp__plugin_flyte_flyte__run_task. It now pairs with flyte-docs and reads as
mcp__plugin_flyte_flyte-cluster__run_task, which also says what the server is for.

Marketplace name -> flyte, plugin version -> 0.3.0, pi package -> 0.0.5. Verified
after the move: claude plugin validate passes, all 5 manifests parse, 15 skills
present, and the local server still serves 0 tools disconnected / 13 connected.

* docs: trim the flyte-mcp-server skill to what only a skill can provide

The skill was written before the plugin bundled anything, so more than half of its
369 lines were setup documentation: how to run the bundled server, its environment
variables, and how to paste `claude mcp add` / opencode.json snippets. That is
reference material for humans and belongs in the README, not in a skill that costs
model context on every Flyte turn.

Cut to 167 lines, keeping the parts nothing else can supply:

- when to drive Flyte through MCP versus the CLI. A model holding 16 MCP tools will
  reach for them by default; no tool description tells it to use the CLI for CI/CD,
  cron, or anything deterministic.
- building and deploying a server of your own, and scoping it with tool groups,
  explicit tool lists, and allowlists. That is code generation, which is what skills
  are for -- and now that internal-flyte-apps is tenant-agnostic, any team can do it.

Deleted the hand-maintained MCP tools table. It duplicated information the running
server already exposes through tools/list, and it had rotted: it listed five tools
removed in flyte-sdk v2.3.6 and two samples passing a `script` tool group that raises.
Anything mirroring the SDK's tool list will rot the same way.

The frontmatter description changed to match, so the skill is now selected for "should
this be MCP or the CLI" and "build me an MCP server" rather than for setup questions
the README answers better.

Moves the configuration reference into the plugin README, and fixes the stale
`flyte` -> `flyte-cluster` server name left in both READMEs after the rename.

* docs: state plainly that only Claude Code gets the MCP servers

The README said the skills were portable across harnesses without ever saying the
MCP servers are not. Someone installing via Codex or Hermes had no way to know they
were getting 15 skills and zero servers, or why.

Adds a per-harness table, and explains the Codex case specifically: Codex plugins
*can* bundle MCP servers via an mcpServers field, but ours would not work there --
.mcp.json locates the local launcher with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, which Codex does not
expand (openai/codex#22842), so the server would fail to start.

Also adds the part that actually helps: every one of these harnesses supports MCP, so
the servers can be wired up by hand. flyte-docs is plain remote HTTP with no auth and
no local dependency, so it drops into Codex, opencode, Hermes and pi in a few lines --
snippets included for each. flyte-cluster needs an absolute path to the launcher,
which stops being true once flyte-sdk#1319 ships and the command becomes
`uvx --from "flyte[mcp]" flyte-mcp --transport stdio`.

Fixes a stale FLYTE_MCP_NO_SEARCH reference left from before that flag was inverted.

* refactor: name the marketplace after the repo, not after the plugin

`/plugin install flyte@flyte` reads as nonsense -- the syntax is plugin@marketplace,
so repeating the same word tells you nothing about which is which. The doubling is
inherited (it was flyte-skills@flyte-skills before the rename); shortening both names
made it more obvious rather than introducing it.

The marketplace is now `flyte-agent-plugins`, matching the repo, so the whole flow
uses one identifier:

  /plugin marketplace add flyteorg/flyte-agent-plugins
  /plugin install flyte@flyte-agent-plugins
  /plugin marketplace remove flyte-agent-plugins

That also fixes a real mismatch: `/plugin marketplace remove` takes the name from
marketplace.json, explicitly "not the source you passed to add". With the old name
users would have added `flyteorg/flyte-agent-plugins` and then had to remove
something called `flyte`.

And it avoids a collision hazard. Marketplace names are globally unique per user --
adding a second marketplace under an existing name replaces the first -- so claiming
a name as generic as `flyte` was asking for trouble. `flyte-agent-plugins` is
specific to this repo.

The plugin itself stays `flyte`: it is the product, and it is what namespaces the
skills (/flyte:flyte-deploy-aws) and the MCP tools.

* docs: say what has to be restarted, not just "restart"

`flyte-cluster` decides its tool set at startup, so the docs told users to restart
after logging in to Flyte -- without saying what. "Restart the server" is not
actionable either: plugin MCP servers are managed through plugin installation, not
/mcp, so there is no per-server restart to reach for.

The answer is `/reload-plugins`, which reconnects a plugin's MCP servers in the
current session, or restarting Claude Code. Now named explicitly in both READMEs, the
launcher's docstring, and the instructions string the model itself reads when the
server comes up disconnected -- that last one matters most, since the model is what
gets asked "why can't you see my runs?".

* fix: remove MCP tool names that never existed, drop the flyte-mcp-server skill

Five skills instructed the model to call `flyte_mcp_list_runs`, `flyte_mcp_get_run`,
`flyte_mcp_run_task` and friends. No such tools exist. The server exposes `list_runs`,
`get_run`, `run_task` -- no prefix -- and clients namespace them further, so Claude
Code actually sees `mcp__plugin_flyte_flyte-cluster__list_runs`. flyte-sdk-run's "Tool
Priority" section told the model to *prefer* these, so it would try them, get
"Unknown tool", and have to recover. flyte-sdk-author additionally advertised
`flyte_mcp_build_image`, a tool removed from the SDK in v2.3.6.

Fixed by describing capabilities instead of naming tools. Any hardcoded name is wrong
for someone -- the namespacing differs per client -- and the server already describes
its own tools and parameters through tools/list, which cannot go stale.

Also deletes the flyte-mcp-server skill. Two things kept it alive and neither holds:

- "Build your own server" is a platform-team job, and the canonical examples are now
  retrievable at runtime: the bundled flyte-docs search returns
  flyte_mcp_app_filtered.py -- the allowlist/scoping example -- from the flyte-sdk
  repo, correct as of flyteorg/flyte-sdk#1319 and current as the SDK evolves.
- "When to use MCP vs the CLI" mostly guarded a non-problem. MCP tools are not
  reachable from a shell script, so a model writing CI has no wrong option to pick,
  and it cannot call tools that do not exist for config or log streaming. The one
  real failure mode is the opposite -- shelling out when MCP is available -- and
  flyte-sdk-run's Tool Priority already covers it.

The skill was also written to help users decide things the plugin now decides for
them: search ships enabled, the cluster server auto-detects, transports are settled.

14 skills, one less hand-maintained tool list in the repo.

directory -- Codex reads it for user and project skills, Hermes reads it

since the flag is what a reader needs, and says plainly that `--target

feat: run the published flyte-mcp CLI instead of a local wrapper

The plugin shipped `plugins/flyte/scripts/flyte_mcp_stdio.py` for two reasons,
both now gone:

1. `flyte[mcp]` <= 2.5.11 silently served HTTP even with `--transport stdio`
   (flyteorg/flyte-sdk#1319). Fixed — stdio speaks JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout.
2. The CLI had no way to pick a tool set. It now has `--tool-groups`, `--tools`,
   and `--read-only`, and reads FLYTE_MCP_PROJECT / FLYTE_MCP_DOMAIN.

So `.mcp.json` launches the SDK's own entry point straight from PyPI:

    uvx --from "flyte[mcp]>=2.5.18" flyte-mcp --transport stdio \
      --tool-groups task,run,action,logs,app,trigger,project,secret,condition,identity

`>=2.5.18` is the first release capping `mcp<2`. Without the cap `mcp` 2.0.0
resolves, `mcp.server.fastmcp` is gone, and the server dies at import reporting
the misleading "mcp is not installed". The three `search` groups are left out on
purpose: the hosted `flyte-docs` server already provides them, and enabling them
shallow-clones a ~120 MB corpus into `~/.flyte/mcp` on first launch.

Dropping the wrapper drops the `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` path with it, so
`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` can finally carry the MCP servers — openai/codex#22842
no longer applies when there is nothing to expand. The key is `mcpServers`, not
the `mcp_servers` the Codex docs show; the manifest struct is camelCase
(openai/codex#22105).

One behaviour change worth knowing: the CLI registers its control-plane tools
unconditionally, where the wrapper hid them until a cluster was reachable. The
server still starts with no Flyte config at all, so the plugin is still usable
while you deploy your first cluster — the tools now fail at call time rather than
being absent, and nothing needs a `/reload-plugins` after you log in.

Verified against the published package: 29 tools register, the server starts with
an empty HOME and no config anywhere, and `list_runs` returns real data with a
cached `flyte` CLI login.

Search previously required the local stdio server to clone ~120 MB of corpus into
~/.flyte/mcp and needed uv and git on PATH. That is a lot of setup for "look up how

deniedMcpServers entry or disabling the plugin.
